Subject: KQL quick tips for Sentinel data lake (new solution for Infoblox, F5, FortiGate FW log centralisation) [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Network team,

I'm reaching out as we have created an Entra ID group to grant access to the Sentinel data lake that will be the replacement for the EDC Syslog-NG StoreBox that you may have used for troubleshooting your network appliances, etc..
I am planning to hold a workshop on querying your log data at some point, but feel free to reach out to myself or the team (via the distribution list CC'd in this email) with any issues or questions.

How to get access?
Group membership to request: AAD_ADMIN_DEWR_Sentinel_Network_Engineer
SNOW form: Access to Resource - Comprehensive - Service Desk Portal<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=96975cc487f0a290824343380cbb3577&table=sc_cat_item>
Example membership request:
[cid:image002.png@01DD0575.7C027030]
Make sure you select the XX1234_a on SharedServicesCentre.onmicrosoft.com or the group will not appear in the group drop down.

Direct link to KQL Queries page: https://security.microsoft.com/lake-explorer?tid=dd0cfd15-4558-4b12-8bad-ea26984fc417

  *   This should be your default place to query the data lake as the integration with the Azure portal will be deprecated by Microsoft early next year.
  *   Alternative in the Azure portal: https://portal.azure.com/#@SharedServicesCentre.onmicrosoft.com/resource/subscriptions/a36e344a-5d12-47cf-bada-af5a7539cb5a/resourceGroups/CORE-AUEA-SOC/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/core-ala-auea-stn/logs

Screenshot of the KQL Queries page:
[cid:image003.png@01DD0575.7C027030]
Note the highlighted in red drop down. After logging in to this portal you will need to make sure to select the available scopes or your query will fail.


Official Microsoft KQL resources:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/data-explorer/kql-learning-resources
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/kusto/query/?view=microsoft-sentinel&preserve-view=true
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/azure/sentinel/datalake/kql-queries
For anyone familiar with SQL this is an SQL --> KQL cheat sheet from Microsoft<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/sql-cheat-sheet?view=microsoft-sentinel>
For anyone familiar with Splunk this is a Splunk --> KQL cheat sheet from Microsoft<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/splunk-cheat-sheet?view=microsoft-sentinel>

Non-Microsoft resources:
https://github.com/rod-trent/MustLearnKQL (YouTube series found here: 1. Must Learn KQL: Introduction<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rcy2uSMLyqo>, PDF version attached)

All searches of the data lake cost money determined by the total data searched (in GB). While this is relatively inexpensive for short timeframes it will quickly increase when including a wide time range (e.g., searching across 24h is significantly cheaper than 30 days) so please be cautious.
Reach out directly to the distribution list CC'd on this email for specific advice on KQL query efficiency!

Example Queries:

// Table name and stop query after 10 results to see what data is available.
CommonSecurityLog_DL_CL
| limit 10

// Line 1: Table name
// Line 2: Filter based on the time window
// Line 3: count number of events based on the application protocol field
// Line 4: order the results by the _count field (output of line 3)
CommonSecurityLog_DL_CL
| where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-05-26) .. datetime(2026-05-27))
| summarize count() by ApplicationProtocol
| order by count_ desc

//Keyword search
// Line 1: Table name
// Line 2: return results where the string "cyber.gov.au" is present anywhere in the event
// Line 3: stop querying after returning 100 results
ASimDnsActivityLogs_DL_CL
| search "cyber.gov.au"
| limit 100

// Line 1: Table name (destination for EDC F5 log events)
// Line 2: limit results based on virtual server
// Line 3: return 10 events from the full results of the query (as the name suggest, a good way to get a sample of event results without returning thousands and thousands of results from a broad query)
ASimWebSessionLogs_DL_CL
| where AdditionalFields.vserver == "ESG/EDC_ESG_I1_http_virtual"
| sample 10


Feel free to play around once you have membership in AAD_ADMIN_DEWR_Sentinel_Network_Engineer, if everything works how I hope then you won't be able to query tables not relevant to your roles.

Again, please reach out to me or the team if you have questions or problems with access.

Good Morning Claudia
The Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Team is seeking your feedback on a new Information Management Awareness training course that will replace the existing Information Management - Education course currently available on Learnhub. We are contacting you as our team consulted you regarding the Information Management Policy, approved September 2025, and would like to seek your views on the following

  *   Course content is not in conflict with any information that your team advises staff on

  *   Alignment with your current practices, systems and policies in particular if there is any missing information that could affect users in the Department of Education

  *   Relevance and usefulness of knowledge check examples and scenarios

  *   Any gaps or areas for improvement

Our team is consulting teams in both DEWR and Department of Education areas for feedback.
We would appreciate your feedback on the following two documents

  *   Information Management Awareness course
  *   Knowledge Check Scenario Questions
Please review the two attached documents and provide feedback by COB Friday 26 June 2026. Send your feedback to: informationmanagementinbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:informationmanagementinbox@dewr.gov.au>
What's changing?
The new course has been designed to reflect current policies, practices and expectations, and to provide a more engaging and practical learning experience for staff. The content has interactive elements and aligns with the updated Information Management Policy (approved September 2025).
Purpose of the new course
The Information Management Awareness course aims to:

  *   Provides a streamlined learning experience, approximately 30 minutes including knowledge check questions).
  *   Strengthen staff understanding of their responsibilities in managing information.
  *   Promote good practice in creating, storing, securing and disposing of information. Support compliance with legislative and policy requirements.
  *   Supports compliance with legislative and policy requirements with information across the department.
Thank you for your time and input.

Dear Schools and Youth Group

The Privacy (Australian Government Agencies — Governance) APP Code 2017<https://www.legislation.gov.au/Series/F2017L01396> (Privacy Code) requires the department to maintain an up-to-date record of its personal information holdings (the Register). In line with the department's [?pdf icon]   Privacy Management Plan<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/edu-legal/DeptDocs/Privacy%20Management%20Plan%202025-26.pdf> the department reviews the Register at least annually. The Corporate and Information Law Team is responsible for coordinating this review by seeking input from each Group in the department.

Please see attached the Guidelines for the Personal Information Holdings Register which includes further information about the Register, the process for updating it and your role in this process.

For action: Reviewing and updating the Register

The attached Register includes the input from the Schools and Youth Group in the 2025 Register. We would be grateful if you could circulate this Register to the Branches in your Group and ask them to review the existing entries for currency, add any new entries and mark any entries no longer held by the department.

It would be helpful if any updates could be provided using track changes so we can easily see any updates. As you will see from the attached Register, personal information holdings could include databases, electronic systems or programs that collect personal information of individuals, including staff. If the holding does not include personal information (e.g. it is all de-identified data), this does not need to be included.

Contracted service providers

Personal information collected by contracted service providers will need to be included if the department holds the information. The Australian Privacy Principles Guidelines<https://www.oaic.gov.au/agencies-and-organisations/app-guidelines/chapter-b-key-concepts#holds> state that 'holds' includes where the department has physical possession of a record containing personal information and can access that information physically or by use of an electronic device, or where the department has the right or power to deal with the personal information, even if the department does not physically possess or own the medium on which the personal information is stored.

Timeframe

We would be grateful if you could please review and update the attached Register for your Group by COB Tuesday, 7 July 2026. Please return the updated register by this date to Privacy@education.gov.au<mailto:Privacy@education.gov.au>.

Clearance

All SES officers are responsible for ensuring that the personal information holdings relevant to their Branch's work are included on their Group's Register and are kept accurate, up to date, and complete. At the completion of each annual review, SES officers must confirm that all personal information holdings relevant to their Branch's work are included on the Register for the Group Manager's approval prior to returning the updated Group Register to the Corporate and Information Law Team.

short_description: RE: Information Management Awareness Course - Consultation Draft
description:
Hi team,

Thank you for the opportunity to review the new Information management awareness course. I have made some comments and suggestions for your consideration.

I did note that the training doesn’t mention appropriately classifying/ marking documents (and ensuring correct, storage, disposal etc.). Given we work on a Protected network and the vast majority of information staff are producing, should be, at a minimum Official, I think it would be worthwhile to reference this in the course. I’ve provided some words below for your consideration and inclusion if appropriate.

All staff must ensure information is correctly classified and clearly marked when it is created, in line with the Australian Governments Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF)<https://www.protectivesecurity.gov.au/> and supporting departmental guidance<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/dewr-emergency/SitePages/Information-Handling.aspx>. Classification determines how information is stored, shared and disposed of. Apply markings such as OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED consistently in documents and systems.

Information classified as PROTECTED or above requires stricter handling controls, including use of approved systems, limited access on a need?to?know basis and secure disposal. Always follow departmental guidance<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/sites/dewr-emergency/SitePages/Information-Handling.aspx> for storing, transmitting and destroying classified material. Seek advice from the Protective Security team <mailto:protective.security@dewr.gov.au>  if you have any questions.

Please let me know if you have any questions or would like to discuss further.

Thanks,
Caitlin

Caitlin Nedeljkovic
Assistant Director, Security Governance

short_description: Re: Information Management Awareness Course - Consultation Draft - Lex 59891
description:
Hi Information Management and Sharepoint Team,

As requested, we have reviewed the Information Management Awareness Module from an information law perspective. We have the following comments:

  *   The module does not currently provide any details of the legal framework for record retention, which we suggest is useful to ensure that staff have a good understanding of their legal obligations, such as:
     *   What is a Commonwealth record subject to retention obligations under the Archives Act 1983 (Archives Act)
     *   The offence for destruction, disposal, transfer, damage or alteration of Commonwealth records in section 24(1) of the Archives Act
     *   When such conduct is authorised under section 24(2) of the Archives Act.
  *   The module refers to discarding of 'Redundant, Obsolete, and Trivial' information. We suggest making it clearer the link to section 24(2)(c) of the Archives Act, which authorises disposal of Commonwealth records in accordance with normal administrative practice.
  *   In relation to the sections on access and use, we suggest the module make clear that the Privacy Act 1988 and secrecy provisions may impose additional restrictions on who is authorised to access or use information than what is required from an information management perspective.
  *   In relation to the section on dispose, it does not appear to be completely consistent with the ability of staff to dispose of records in accordance with normal administrative practice.
  *   In relation to the section on 'Protect information when required', we suggest making clear that this aligns with the department's obligation under Australian Privacy Principle 11.1 to take reasonable steps to protect personal information from 'misuse, interference and loss; and from unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.
  *   In relation to the section on 'Include the important details' you may want to make clear that these actions can assist the department in being able to efficiently undertake searches for documents subject to FOI or privacy requests.
  *   We suggest including details of the privacy and security risks in retaining records for longer than is necessary, and encouraging the destruction of records as soon as it is authorised under the Archives Act. It could also be noted that there is another benefit in that once they have been destroyed, records can no longer be subject to an FOI request.
  *   You may want to add a question to the knowledge check scenarios related to the legal obligations.

If you have any other questions, feel free to contact me.

Regards,

Dilani Ponniah
Principal Government Lawyer (and Privacy Officer)

  *   Relevance and usefulness of knowledge check examples and scenarios

The new course has been designed to reflect current policies, practices and expectations, and to provide a more engaging and practical learning experience for staff. The content has interactive elements and aligns with the updated Information Management Policy (approved September 2025).
Purpose of the new course
The Information Management Awareness course aims to:

  *   Provides a streamlined learning experience, approximately 30 minutes including knowledge check questions).
  *   Strengthen staff understanding of their responsibilities in managing information.
  *   Promote good practice in creating, storing, securing and disposing of information. Support compliance with legislative and policy requirements.
  *   Supports compliance with legislative and policy requirements with information across the department.

Hello Service Desk,

Could you please log a job to Platform Services?

Hi Platform Services.

The EBIW (DEWR on-premises Data Warehouse), has a mechanism that is triggered each night to robocopy extract files (from MTP production system) to our lower environments and to a Production Audit server.

For the last 10+ years (on differing servers), and up until 18/06), it had been working fine.

It is now taking a very long time to run and only copying a subset of files to the target servers (when it does run).

Could you please investigate and fix what was patched on 18/06?

I cant see anything particular in the Windows logs, although I am seeing a large number of SenseNdr.exe errors (Windows Defender).

Losing server is EPRESQL031V01 (EPRESQL031S01/EPRESQL031S03).

Gaining servers are EDEESQL023, EPPESQL024, EPRESQL326.

The robocopy job copies from the Production J Drive, CDSDATA subfolders to the gaining server's J Drive, CDSDATA subfolders.

While the lack of file copy to the lower environments is annoying, the file copy to the AUDIT Production server is causing problems for forensic analysis, and I am being asked questions about where the data is.

Cheers,

David.

ps I have spoken to the Airlock team and they pointed me to Platform Services.

Currently we've been advised there are issues with Workforce Australia in PreProd. It appears that ADFS in Prod is looking for an issuer/signer of the payload referencing the old SSC CA for PreProd.

I've attempted re-installing the full chain into the Trusted Root Certification Authorities store in both PreProd and Prod but the issue still persists.

To fix these issues, our ADFS PreProd environment requires a five year token-signing and token-encryption certificate using the internal Australian Government Construction CA.

These certificate are used to sign issued tokens or decrypt incoming tokens, and operate exclusively at the low application layer for claims-based authentication. It is not used for securing outer SSL/TLS transport channels.

short_description: Request for review of Microsoft Teams deletion guidance and controls
description:
Hi team,

I am writing to request a review of the current DEWR guidance and controls<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0017115> relating to the deletion of Microsoft Teams sites across the shared tenancy.
This request follows a recent incident involving the deletion of an FWO Team site (FWO - Business Analysis Community of Practice), which has since been restored. While we understand changes are being made to the Group Decommission request form, we have identified broader concerns with the current guidance and user-led deletion process.

Background
Current guidance directs users to delete Teams sites themselves when they are no longer required. While this reflects standard Microsoft functionality, this approach does not align with FWO information governance requirements.

Key issues identified

  *   Deleting a Team removes the associated Microsoft 365 Group and access to all related content and collaboration context (including files, channel conversations and linked services).
  *   Following deletion, FWO Information Management does not have visibility of the site or its contents and is unable to assess whether business records existed or whether appropriate recordkeeping actions were taken.
  *   While some content may be retained under platform retention policies, this does not preserve records in their original context or ensure they can be appropriately managed or disposed of in line with agency requirements.


This creates a risk that business records may be deleted without appropriate review or authorisation. We also note that the current knowledge article and process appear to apply tenancy-wide and do not account for agency-specific governance requirements.
In particular:

  *   FWO uses Teams to support its core business functions (which can include Taskforces, operations and investigations teams).
  *   FWO requires Information Management oversight prior to disposal of Microsoft Teams.
  *   disposal decisions for FWO information must be made in accordance with FWO governance and legislative obligations.

Request
We request that DEWR review the current approach and consider the following:

  *   Updating the knowledge article to remove or amend advice that users can directly delete Teams sites, and instead direct agencies to follow their own Information Management processes.
  *   Implementing controls, where feasible, to restrict or prevent user-initiated deletion of Teams sites without appropriate review or approval.
  *   Ensuring shared tenancy processes and guidance clearly account for agency-specific governance requirements.
  *   Clarifying responsibility for disposal decision-making for Teams content across participating agencies.

We are happy to work with DEWR to support a consistent and compliant approach across the tenancy.
Please let me know if further information is required or if this request should be progressed via a different channel.



Regards,

description:
Hi Information Management

I will start with the question and then some information about where we are

The Question : How long do we need to keep digital documents relating to Jobseekers in our Employment Systems?

The Details
We have documents relating to many things in a single database called Document Store which was designed to be the central place to store documents for Jobseekers and Providers.

This database is of concern as we have never cleaned up anything from it.

Document Store DB
Current size        : 15 TB
Oldest record    : 23 years old


It currently holds 87 million documents some dating back to 2003 and TSD have already detailed that they are no longer performing database maintenance tasks on this database due to its size.

I am keen to get some archiving done on this database but I do run into resistance from project teams as they do not want to remove a document that they feel may be needed by someone at some stage.

I would like to understand what the legal requirement is for us to retain documents in this DB.

My aim would be to take a full backup of this DB and have the backup available in a Read Only offline capacity for Production support enquires, and then Delete all documents for the active online database that we are not legally bound to keep... ie > 7 years... if we do not need to keep these on the active online system? They would still be available if needed in the offline backup that Production Support would have access to.....   Well the next question -  Do we actually need to keep them at all after 7 years?

short_description: CD Batch Jobs failing to communicate with SAPPI Services on new Windows 2022 Servers
description:
Hello, please forward this to an appropriate team for investigation.

Affected Servers:
- EDEIAPP214SA
- EDEIAPP214SB
- EPPIAPP200SA
- EPPIAPP200SA
- EPPIAPP205SA
- EPPIAPP205SB

Batch Job accounts:
- ServiceAutoSys_D
- ServiceAutoSys_P

We have observed that our Corporate Directory batch jobs have been unable to communicate with the SAP PI Services in the lower environment. This appeared to begin after CD was migrated onto new Windows 2022 servers. However, the issue has also began occurring on the Windows 2019 servers last Friday (12th of June).
SDO had notified us that they stopped receiving lower-environment CD communications from our batch jobs, which has prompted this investigation.

Batch Job Error (PreProd W2022):
System.ServiceModel.EndpointNotFoundException: There was no endpoint listening at https://pitest.sap.hosts.network/XISOAPAdapter/MessageServlet?senderParty=&senderService=DEEWR_CD&receiverParty=&receiverService=&interface=DEEWR_Employee_OUT&interfaceNamespace=http%3A%2F%2Fdeewr.gov.au%2Fglobal%2Fpi that could accept the message. This is often caused by an incorrect address or SOAP action. See InnerException, if present, for more details. ---> System.Net.WebException: Unable to connect to the remote server ---> System.Net.Sockets.SocketException: A connection attempt failed because the connected party did not properly respond after a period of time, or established connection failed because connected host has failed to respond 10.11.240.152:443

A different error occurs on the Windows 2019 PreProd and W2022 Dev servers:
System.ServiceModel.Security.SecurityNegotiationException: Could not establish trust relationship for the SSL/TLS secure channel with authority 'pitest.sap.hosts.network'. ---> System.Net.WebException: The underlying connection was closed: Could not establish trust relationship for the SSL/TLS secure channel. ---> System.Security.Authentication.AuthenticationException: The remote certificate is invalid according to the validation procedure.

short_description: RE: Video conferencing set up for Belinda Campbell meeting room (06.050) | FAS for the Labour Market & Industry Policy Division, Employment & Workforce Group
description:
Good morning,

Thanks for getting back to me. Please see the requested business case below.

This business case seeks approval to install video conferencing (VC) equipment in a Senior Executive Band 2 (SEB2) office, noting that this is an exception to the Department's Accommodation Principles. Under current policy, VC equipment is only installed in SESB3 (or equivalent Public Office Holder) offices, and as such, a formal business case is required for any deviation.

At present, the absence of VC capability in SEB2 offices limits the ability to effectively participate in virtual meetings from within the office. This creates inefficiencies, as alternative meeting spaces with VC functionality must be sourced, which may not always be readily available or suitable. As a result, this can delay meetings, disrupt workflows, and reduce productivity, particularly where there is a need for frequent or time-sensitive virtual engagement.

The proposed installation of VC equipment in the SEB2 office would address these limitations by enabling seamless participation in virtual meetings directly from the office. This would support more efficient day-to-day operations, improve responsiveness, and enhance collaboration with internal and external stakeholders. It would also align with the increasing reliance on virtual engagement across the Department.

Consistent with departmental guidance, when the office is not in use by the occupant, it would be made available for staff use as a meeting room. This would maximise the value of the investment by increasing access to VC-enabled spaces and supporting broader team needs for hybrid meetings.

The risks associated with this proposal are minimal and relate primarily to the precedent of approving VC installations outside of policy settings. However, this can be managed by clearly documenting the operational need and ensuring appropriate approval is obtained from the Chief Operating Officer.
It is recommended that approval be granted to install VC equipment in the SEB2 office to support operational efficiency and improved meeting capability. I would be grateful if you could please forward this business case to the relevant Chief Operating Officer for consideration and approval.

Emma Keneally

description:
Dear Service Desk team,

I am writing to request that Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) be made available for installation via the Company Portal (CP) for our user accounts (users copied in cc and more details provided below). SSMS is already listed on ASQA's Approved Software List (ASL), but it does not currently appear as an option in our Company Portal profiles for self-service installation. Having SSMS available in the CP will enable our team to install it promptly and proceed with critical database script analysis required for our project. It would be great if you can enable the latest version of SQL Server Management Studio 2020<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal?id=form&table=cmdb_software_product_model&sys_id=6e9c00e61baab410e6790fabdc4bcb46&view=sp> available from the Approved Software list.

Context / Justification: Our team is undertaking Phase 2 pre-work for the ASQA | PS Slingshot project. This involves analysing a large number of legacy SQL database objects (including ~61 stored procedures and over 686 scripts) to understand underlying tables, views, synonyms, and data flows. We have already been granted access to the relevant pre-production database (APP_ASQA_ASQANET_SQL_PREPROD) via the Service Desk Portal. However, without a suitable database client, we cannot fully utilise this access to query the database and inspect sample data. SSMS, being an officially approved software, is the ideal tool for us to carry out this analysis effectively.

Request: Considering the above, could you please publish or enable SSMS in our Company Portal profiles as soon as possible so that we can install it on our devices? This will allow us to immediately begin the database analysis for Phase 2. The user IDs and associated emails for the three team members who require SSMS are as follows:

description:
Hey team,

One of my lot has raised some questions on the CyberArk Vault below, and we were hoping to get some clarification.

Happy to organise a quick chat if that'll be easier.

Cheers
Liam

From: DE SILVA,Casey
Sent: Thursday, 21 May 2026 11:47 AM
To: WILLIAMSON,Ash <Ash.Williamson@dewr.gov.au<mailto:Ash.Williamson@dewr.gov.au>>
Cc: WILSON,Liam <Liam.Wilson@dewr.gov.au<mailto:Liam.Wilson@dewr.gov.au>>; DUDAGA,Prem <Prem.Dudaga@dewr.gov.au<mailto:Prem.Dudaga@dewr.gov.au>>
Subject: RE: Clarification on Emergency Access Procedure – Broadcom VMware Environment (SSP Annex Ref: 1610) [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Ash,

I hope you're doing well. Many thanks for sharing the documentation and for your support.
I've had a chance to review it and wanted to share my understanding.

I was able to identify three distinct recovery scenarios:

  1.  CyberArk Vault is online, but some or all component servers are unavailable (PSM, PSMPs, PVWA, CPM, CCP).
  2.  CyberArk Vault and PVWA are online, but other component servers are unavailable (PSM, PSMPs, CPM, CCP).
  3.  CyberArk Vault and all component servers are offline.

From my understanding, in the first two scenarios we would temporarily revert from Duo multi-factor authentication to CyberArk authentication.
This would allow users to access systems using emergency credentials via distributed passwords and split delivery methods.

In the third scenario, where all components are offline, access would rely on extracted offline passwords or securely stored hardcopy credentials maintained in a secure vault.
While going through the material, I had a few questions and would appreciate your guidance:


  *   The hosting team typically accesses the Broadcom/VMware hosting environment through various jump servers, retrieving privileged credentials from CyberArk. In case of a CyberArk service disruption, I understand that the Cyber team can disable MFA so that access is limited to username and password, could you please confirm if this is the standard approach?
  *   Could you please clarify the password rotation timelines for service accounts and administrator accounts in such scenarios?
  *   What are the defined RTO and RPO targets for recovery, particularly if CyberArk is compromised and cannot be restored promptly?
  *   Are offline password copies kept in sync with CyberArk password rotations and Active Directory updates?
     *   Alternatively, are there designated accounts with longer rotation cycles that can be used to regain administrative access and reset other credentials? (I understand this may be more complex for service accounts.)
  *   Is there an established workflow outlining how these events are triggered, along with escalation paths for teams like ours?

I appreciate your time and guidance on these points.

Kind regards,
Casey

Plan for June 20th Server Migration Release

short_description: DRAFT OSCA to training product mapping now available
description:
Dear web service users

This email is to let you know that the DRAFT OSCA to training product mapping (attached) is now available in sandbox. This includes the following changes:

  *   all current ANZCO Identifier’s now have an end date of 30 June 2026
  *   every training package product that had an ANZCO Identifier now has an OSCA Identifier with a start of 1 July 2026
  *   TGA Sandbox (https://tgastaging.training.gov.au<https://tgastaging.training.gov.au/>) shows both the ANZCO Identifier and OSCA Identifier.

This mapping is to support system testing and integration and is not to be used for any formal reporting. Inclusion of draft mapping builds on the previous work to release the new OSCA classification schemes and values to sandbox which was completed on 1 May 2026.

This email is simply an early heads-up only on the sandbox progress and noting that nothing is changing in production yet. The goal is to give you time to check that your system is ready for the full implementation in the production environment on 1 January 2027.

Important dates

  *   1 May 2026 (DONE) - The new OSCA classification scheme and the reference data (only) were added to sandbox.
  *   15 June 2026 (DONE) - OSCA to training product mapping (draft) data was added to sandbox.
  *   From 1 January 2027 - OSCA scheme, reference data and mapping (final) to training product data will be available in production.

What you need to know / do

  *   You should have already confirmed your system can accept the new OSCA data scheme name and reference data and continue to work without errors (more information attached).
  *   From 15 June, check that your system can:
     *   accept the new OSCA to training product mapping (draft) data.
     *   continue working without errors when the new classification values are returned.
  *   Your existing SOAP integrations will continue to work as they do today.
  *   We will continue to communicate with you as 1 January 2027 approaches for the data to be available in production.
Background information
OSCA<https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/classifications/osca-occupation-standard-classification-australia/latest-release> is a new Australian Bureau of Statistics occupational classification that will replace ANZSCO. OSCA classifications will be assigned to qualifications, specialisations and AQF?level accredited courses. Full implementation in the production environment is scheduled to be available from 1 January 2027. The ABS will update OSCA in the years following. When updates occur, NCVER will update OSCA reference data and any existing assigned classifications in the National Training Register.

NCVER update on the transition from ANZSCO to OSCA training products
NCVER is in the process of assigning OSCA codes to all nationally recognised qualifications/courses based on their current ANZSCO codes. This information will be available on the National Training Register (training.gov.au) from 1 January 2027. Contact your state/territory training authority in 2027 for information about the OSCA code for any government funded locally recognised courses that you deliver.

Support
If you have any connection issues when OSCA reference data appears in sandbox, please contact TGA Help<mailto:tgahelp@dewr.gov.au>.

Kind regards

The TGA Project Team
Australian Government
Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
www.training.gov.au<http://www.training.gov.au/>
The help desk operates during business hours

short_description: URGENT ADVICE REQUIRED FOR FOI REQUEST
description:
Hi

I am writing to seek your urgent assistance, if possible, in locating records required for an FOI request.

A child care provider has requested regulatory documents relating to their approval in 2007/2008.  The FOI request relates to the child care provider 3Apples.

As you may be aware, the Australian Government is not responsible for regulatory approval and the provider's FOI request was referred to the Victorian regulatory agency - Victorian Early Childhood Regulatory Authority (VECRA).

VECRA have advised that child care accreditation in 2007/2008 was the responsibility of the National Childcare Accreditation Council (NCAC) which was a Commonwealth body of the, then, Department of Education, Employment & Workplace Relations.  The NCAC became the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority (ACECQA) in 2012. NCAC child care accreditation documents prior to 2012 were either:

-       transferred to the National Archives of Australia (NAA).  NCAC had an approved Records Authority under the Archives Act 1983, which required certain records to be retained as national archives and transferred to the NAA

      or

-       retained by the DEEWR's by the successor portfolio agency, the Commonwealth Department of Education.


Question
*       Is it possible to search the archived records of the Department relating to the NCAC agency pertaining to the NCAC in the years 2007/2008?
*       If so, what is the process for locating these records?

short_description: Guidance Required – Vault Naming & Credential Strategy for TM1 Databases
description:
Hi Cyber Security Services,

I’m seeking your guidance on implementing a control related to administrator credential management for our IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) environments.

We currently operate three environments:

1. Development
2. Preproduction
3. Production

Each environment contains the same set of 10 databases:

- CORP_APPS
- EDU_BMS
- EDU_FIN_ADM
- EDU_GEUS
- EWR_BMS
- EWR_FIN_ADM
- EWR_GEUS
- HAROLD
- TM1_Config
- VET_ASQA_BMS

As part of a risk treatment (R5 – unauthorised sharing and misuse of administrator accounts), we are required to:

1. Ensure inbuilt administrator account passwords are regularly rotated
2. Store credentials in a secure vault
3. Implement a unique password per database

This results in 30 unique credentials across all environments. :(

Proposed Approach
-----------------------
To support this requirement, I am proposing a vault naming convention that uniquely identifies each database instance by environment and database name. For example:

DEV_CORP_APPS
PREPROD_CORP_APPS
PROD_CORP_APPS

This pattern would be applied consistently across all databases.

Could you please advise on the following:
1. Naming Convention
- Is the proposed <ENV>_<DATABASE_NAME> format acceptable for vault entries?
- Are there any existing standards we should align with?

2. Credential Strategy
- Do you agree with maintaining one unique admin credential per database per environment (30 total)?
- Or would you recommend an alternative approach (e.g., per environment or per platform)?

3. Policy Alignment
- Does this approach meet the Department’s Service Account Policy requirements for privileged account management?

4. Operational Considerations
- Any recommendations regarding rotation frequency, access controls, or auditing for these credentials?
- Is it possible for Corporate Directory staff to manage a Planning Analytics vault where we can register the database instances and generate a password?

FYI these database accounts are not service accounts, they are internal administrator accounts within Planning Analytics.

Thanks,
Elvis

description:
Good morning

We hope this email finds you well.

We are reaching out to request your assistance with setting up some IT equipment and internet connection for an in-person meeting we are holding on 17/18 August, at room 002 - 50 Marcus Clarke Street.

One Board member will be dialling in from interstate, and we will have consultants with presentations on external laptops that will need to be plugged in.
Considering this, we were hoping that you would have the availability some point in the week commencing 10 August to show us how to set up the teams meeting in the meeting room, to ensure that we know how to check that the sound and everything is working?

Additionally,  we will have around 15 external members attending (including Board members, and consultants). The Board members use Board books that will require internet access. Would it be possible for you to please provide a series of login codes to the internet for them?

For background, the following executives/ Minister will be in attendance:

  *   Meg Brighton (Deputy Secretary), and Caitlin Delaney (FAS) have been invited to attend on both days.
  *   Chris Davern (AS) and Jane Mitchell (AS), will be delivering presentations on both days
  *   Minister Clare (TBC)
  *   6 Members of the NSRB Board (all for interstate)
  *   External consultants from Deloitte

Thank you in advance for your assistance.

Please let me know your availability in the week commencing 10 August and I will circulate a meeting invite.

Do not hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or concerns.

description:
Hi team,

[cid:image001.png@01DCF9BC.17E62980]


I found an article from Pait Group<https://www.paitgroup.com/blog/multiple-lines-of-text-fields-in-sharepoint-the-reason-for-the-255-limit> that suggests if I change the column settings option 'Allow Unlimited length in document libraries' to Yes it will fix the problem. [cid:image002.png@01DCF9BE.632788B0]

short_description: Security of Adobe Acrobat Pro DC
description: I'm updating the FOI Guidelines. In the current version we refer to a 2019 report by the Australian Cyber Security Centre which tested the redaction functionality of Adobe Acrobat Pro DC 2017 and reported that the tools permanently deleted the required information so that it was not present in any form in the redacted PDF file when used properly. The report is no longer available on the ACSC website. I assume Adobe continue to update their products to meet current security threats and that it is not possible for anyone to 'undo' redactions applied using Adobe Pro. I wonder whether you have done work in this area and if so, whether we can continue to recommend that agencies use Adobe Pro to redact information from documents.

Updates to EU duties, taxes and fees 









 Dear Karen,



Thank you for choosing Australia Post as your delivery partner. We're writing to let you know about some changes that will affect the way you send parcels to the European Union (EU).

What's changing?

From 1 July 2026, the EU is removing the EUR150 de minimis threshold, which means low-value parcels (under EUR150) entering the EU will now be subject to a flat-rate EUR3 customs duty (per item, not parcel).


It must be noted that the EUR3 customs duty will be applied in addition to the Value Added Tax (VAT) and that 'gift' will no longer be a valid export reason for business senders.

These updates have been designed to help deliver a more consistent application of duties and taxes across all EU member states.

How will these costs be calculated?

As the sender, you'll need to nominate who will be responsible for paying any duties, taxes and fees (referred to as 'landed costs'). The available options are:


	- Receiver pays – charges are paid by the recipient at the destination
	- Sender pays (via Zonos(r) Verified Account) – charges are paid upfront by the sender
	- Sender pays (via Tax ID) – charges are managed externally via the sender's tax arrangement.
Please note that for some destinations, the payment method may be mandated, and the appropriate option will be automatically applied.

If Zonos(r) is used, it will support the calculation, collection and remittance of these landed costs.

Please note, this 'receiver vs sender' payment option process also applies to parcels sent to the US, Canada, Norway and the United Kingdom (UK).

Additional requirements

To comply with these regulatory changes, you'll also need to provide:

	- More detailed customs information, including item classification and country of origin
	- A valid export reason as 'gift' will no longer be accepted for business shipments
	- Accurate declarations as duties may be calculated per item rather than per parcel.
Australia Post system and platform updates

If you're using MyPost Business or Parcel Send, you'll start to see enhancements designed to support these changes, including:

	- Visibility of estimated duties and taxes prior to lodgement
	- Clear prompts to select who will pay the landed costs
	- Options to provide an Importer Tax ID where required.

In your email to Chris Mumford at 12:42pm on 20 May 2026 (first attachment) you note that:

  *   the Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre Inc was incorporated as the Aboriginal Information Service in November 1973 and renamed the Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre in August 1977.

The legal entity, the Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre Inc, operated the Tasmanian Aboriginal Children's Centre: see  About us - Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre<https://tacinc.com.au/about-us/>

In your email to us below, you note that:


  *   the Commonwealth funded the Aboriginal Tutorial Assistance Scheme (ATAS) (later the Indigenous Tutorial Assistance Scheme), which ran from 1989 to 2004 and



  *   under ATAS, the Commonwealth contracted registered tutors to provide assistance to nominated students or groups of students, or at Commonwealth-registered homework centres.



Our first question is whether the Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre Inc. was one of the Commonwealth-registered homework centres at which tutors who were contracted by the Commonwealth under ATAS provided assistance?



Yes, the Tasmanian Aboriginal Children's Centre operated as an Aboriginal Homework Centre in 1995. However, I cannot confirm that it operated as an Aboriginal Homework Centre prior to 1995 (noting the plaintiff's claim that he attended between 1990 and 1993).



Only one file (ES02/09529) was identified as relating to the Centre's operation as a Homework Centre, and this file was created in connection with a specific debt issue.

Indicates that administrative responsibility for staffing and tutor engagement sat outside the Commonwealth; therefore, any records relating to employment or engagement at the Centre would most likely be held at the state/territory or local level, not by the Department

Is this inconsistent with what you have said about the Commonwealth contracting tutors under ATAS?


Yes, that is inconsistent.



Pip McKellar's advice was given without the benefit of the Program Guidelines (they weren't in content manager) and while searches were ongoing. Subject: RE: Inquiry: Status and Process for Formalising Qualtrics Data Retention & Collection Policy [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Josh

Here are my updates.

Following up on our Teams discussion regarding appropriate information management within Qualtrics, we are seeking confirmation, advice, and any supporting resources on the following points:


  *   Recordkeeping:
Qualtrics is not an approved system for long-term data storage. Data generated or collected in Qualtrics which meets the definition of an Information Asset<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/:b:/r/sites/DESE-InformationManagement/Shared%20Documents/Understanding-Information-Assets.pdf?csf=1&web=1&e=SOZxwr> be exported and stored in an approved departmental system such as Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint Online.


  *   Data disposal:
Data that is Identified as Redundant, Obsolete or Trivial<https://sharedservicescentre.sharepoint.com/:b:/r/sites/DESE-InformationManagement/Shared%20Documents/Identifying%20and%20Discarding%20ROT%20Information.pdf?csf=1&web=1&e=jBIVvd> does not need to be stored in approved departmental systems can be deleted directly from the platform where appropriate.


  *   Data retention within Qualtrics:
Data should not be retained indefinitely within Qualtrics, and any extended analyses should be conducted outside the platform.


  *   User responsibilities:
Users (and by extension, business areas) are responsible for managing their data in the platform on a periodic basis that aligns with their business practices.
     *   Users should remove all data that meets the definition of an information asset including personal information from the platform every six months. However, more frequent extraction (e.g. monthly) is recommended to minimise the risk of data breaches.  Data that is not an information asset can be deleted when no longer required within the Qualtrics system.
     *   If ongoing storage within Qualtrics is required, such as to utilise analytics across datasets within the system, users should contact CorporateSystemsIntegration@dewr.gov.au<mailto:CorporateSystemsIntegration@dewr.gov.au>.
     *   Business areas remain responsible for managing this process and should not outsource these practices to developers or web service officers supporting the project. These processes should be embedded within business practices to ensure ongoing alignment with Information Management policies and obligations.


  *   Information Management guidance:
Users should seek advice through from the Information Management and SharePoint team when determining where their data should be stored within departmental systems.

Thanks, and have a great day.

Subject: RE: Inquiry: Status and Process for Formalising Qualtrics Data Retention & Collection Policy [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Julie,

Thanks very much for your detailed feedback, to clarify:

Recordkeeping
You're correct in your interpretation, and I agree the wording could be clearer. The intent is to align both statements rather than create a contradiction. Specifically:
The requirement to export data reflects that Qualtrics is not an approved system for long-term storage, so any information that needs to be retained (i.e. meets the definition of an Information Asset) should be exported and stored in an approved departmental system.
Conversely, where data does not meet retention requirements or is no longer required after analysis and reporting, it can be deleted directly from Qualtrics.

Your suggested framing around retaining only information that qualifies as an Information Asset is very helpful. Would you be able to provide or recommend formal wording that aligns with IM policy? I'm happy for any suggested changes to be made directly to my original enquiry below.

User Responsibilities

  1.  Business case process
From a CSI perspective, business cases are reviewed and approved internally to assess whether the proposed use aligns with appropriate use of the platform (primarily from a technical suitability and cost perspective).
  2.  IM Team advice
We're primarily seeking confirmation that the guidance we're proposing reflects appropriate IM practice. In particular, we wanted to validate whether we can (or should) recommend/enforce a minimum six-month cycle for removal of personal information (with business areas remaining responsible).
We'll manage the implementation approach on our end, but want to ensure alignment with IM policy before formalising this.


  1.  Responsibility of business areas vs developers/web services
This is an area where we're also seeking your guidance.
Our current concern is based on observed practice, where business areas:

     *   Engage developers/web services officers to build a Qualtrics project
     *   Then do not take ongoing responsibility for managing the data
     *   Resulting in sensitive/personal information remaining in Qualtrics for extended periods

This often leads to Web Services needing to step in retrospectively to assist with clean-up and compliance.
Our intent with this statement is to reinforce that business areas remain accountable for their data and IM obligations, regardless of who assists in building the solution. We believe clarifying this responsibility will help mitigate the IM risks we're currently seeing.

We'd appreciate your advice on the appropriate framing here.

Kind regards,

Subject: Question about data retention at end of contract

Good Afternoon Information Management Team,

I'm emailing seeking some guidance about data retention/archiving at the end of a contract.  We currently have an engagement with a company called Transitioning Well, who developed and host a website https://smallbusiness.10dayspaidfdvleave.com.au/ to give guidance to small business on the entitlement to 10 days paid family and domestic violence leave. The contract is due to end in November 2026 and there is no further funding available to continue supporting the website. So we are working on a plan to phase it out and re-purpose/archive materials.

Transitioning Well have asked us whether there are any data retention requirements they need to comply with. Under the contract, Transitioning Well own the IP in the materials created - DEWR has a licence to use itWe know the APS needs to comply with the Archives Act and PGPA Act. I've had a look at the contract with Transitioning Well and there's not much in there about records management - only a clause about the supplier not transferring custody of Commonwealth Records without our consent. I've had a look at the Archives Act and it seems that the material prepared for the contract is probably not a Commonwealth Record because it isn't Commonwealth Property (because Transitioning Well owns the IP).

Could you advise us if there are any record keeping/data retention requirements that apply here? Eg: TW need to hold onto copies of the materials created for 7 years. Or in the absence of anything in the contract and the materials meeting any statutory record keeping requirement, is it up to us how we handle the record keeping and archiving? (For your interest, the National Library has partially archived the website on Trove<https://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20251112183854/https:/smallbusiness.10dayspaidfdvleave.com.au/>).

We have copies of things Transitioning Well provided directly to us (quarterly reports, draft content for review etc). But the main output has been the website and its materials (including videos), and things like social media posts and ads to promote the website, which are a little bit tricker to archive.

We appreciate any advice you could give. We're meeting with Transitioning Well next week to discuss so if you could get back to us by Wednesday COB that would be helpful - let us know if that timing works, and happy to discuss.

Hello Peter

I have received the Changes to Commonwealth Data Retention Provisions invitation and look forward to attending.

I had a question I was keen to raise ahead of the meeting, so it did not side track your session.
Could you tell me how your review has considered or been progressed in collaboration with the NAA update to Administrative Functions Disposal Authority (AFDA) V2, consultation and review?

DEWR has been in the process of developing our Data Retention and Disposal Policy for the last eight months, this has been delayed as we await the release of the NAA update to AFDA V2. Consultation and reviewing the Information management section of the AFDA Express Version 2 Functions<https://www.naa.gov.au/information-management/records-authorities/types-records-authorities/afda-express-version-2-functions>, specific to Data Retention and Management started in August 2025. In the attached email reply from NAA the draft document, AFDA Version 2 - Technology and Information Management<https://www.naa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-08/GRA-data-management.pdf>, is due for release in the June/July.

While developing our policy the agency level Information Management legislative restrictions related to the current AFDA V2 have impeded us progressing to a similar data specific risk-based approach outlined in your documents.

My concern is that once both reviews and guidelines are released, in the coming months, they will not align and will require agencies to re-litigate which one to follow or has more wight in policy development.
Noting your comment that, changes to how Commonwealth policy officers develop data retention provisions, as decided by the Attorney-General and the Minister for Home Affairs, may not override the legal obligations of the AFDA.

I look forward to hearing from you.


regards
Phill

Phill O’Connor
Data Assurance & Compliance Manager

Subject: Changes to Commonwealth Data Retention Provisions [SEC=OFFICIAL]


OFFICIAL
Dear colleagues,

We are introducing changes to how Commonwealth policy officers develop data retention provisions, as decided by the Attorney-General and the Minister for Home Affairs.

Please join us for a presentation on Tuesday 16 June, 3–4pm (calendar invite to follow), where we will outline the Data Retention Review that led to these changes and two reference tools for policy officers:

  *   Data retention principles to guide Commonwealth policy development (attached)
  *   Guidance template – managing data retention obligations, to support agencies in preparing clear guidance for industry (attached)

The reference tools will guide policy officers to develop more cyber-secure and privacy-protecting data retention provisions across the Commonwealth.

In addition, the Attorney-General’s Department is working in collaboration with the Office of Parliamentary Counsel to develop best-practice data retention legislative provisions. These will support more consistent legislative drafting across the Commonwealth.

We encourage you to bring any questions about this new principles-based approach, including how it may interact with your existing policy and legislative development processes. You are welcome to extend the invite to any Legislation Liaison Officers or adjacent colleagues who would benefit from the session.

This work is a key initiative under the 2023–2030 Australian Cyber Security Strategy. The Data Retention Review final report is attached for your reference (please note the report and reference tools are currently for Commonwealth vis only).

Kind regards,

description:
Hi team,
Just logging this one through for visibility and support.
We've identified that users who are members of the Intune mobile group and have (or previously had) a departmental mobile device are being impacted by the Conditional Access policy "Restrict access to Department location."

At the moment, this policy is applying to the AppSpace application and is blocking access when users attempt to sign in from personal mobile devices. This means users are currently unable to access AppSpace across both departmental and personal devices, which isn't the intended behaviour.

Impact

Users unable to access AppSpace on personal devices if they are a member of the Intune Mobile group
Inconsistent user experience based on device history
Potential disruption for users relying on cross-device access

Requirement

Could we please exclude the AppSpace application from the "Restrict access to Department location" Conditional Access policy?
AppSpace should be accessible from personal mobile devices in all circumstances, regardless of Intune mobile group membership or prior enrolment status.

description:
As part of Tenable Identity exposure implementation, please grant Service_TenableIEc permission to read as per the vendor instruction attached.

There 2 parts to this: 

1, Grant permission to the Deleted container and Password container,

#Set Service Account
$serviceAccount = Service_TenableIeX@mgt.dis.gov.au

 

#Don't Edit after here
$domain = Get-ADDomain
@($domain.DeletedObjectsContainer, "CN=Password Settings Container,$($domain.SystemsContainer)") | ForEach-Object {
& dsacls $_ /takeownership
& dsacls $_ /g "$($serviceAccount):LCRP" /I:T
}

dsacls "<__DOMAIN_ROOT__>"  /g "<__SERVICE_ACCOUNT__>:CA;Replicating Directory Changes" "<__SERVICE_ACCOUNT__>:CA;Replicating Directory Changes All"Where
o	<__DOMAIN_ROOT__> refers to the Distinguished Name of the root of the domain. Example: DC=<DOMAIN>,DC=<TLD>
o	<__SERVICE_ACCOUNT__> refers to the service account that Tenable Identity Exposure uses. Example: DOMAIN\tenablead.

short_description: Confirmation of After-Hours Contractor Access Card Activation Process
description:
Hi DEWR Security Team,

I am seeking confirmation of the agreed arrangement for the activation of contractor access cards for Fair Work Ombudsman personnel, both during business hours and outside normal operating hours.

Following a recent after hours activation request, it was advised that the Service Desk manages these requests, with after hour support available via the Service Desk on 02 6240 9999 (selecting option 1 - urgent other).

However, during the activation process, DEWR on call staff requested email confirmation from FWO Security before proceeding with the card activation. While this was manageable on the occasion, it may create delays where the responsible security officer is unavailable or unable to provide immediate email confirmation.

To streamline the process, FWO Security would like key personnel responsible for managing security requests to be formally recognised as authorised officers for after hours contractor access card activation requests. Where required, a follow up email can be provided as soon as practicable after the request.

Could you please confirm whether this arrangement can be implemented and advise of any requirements from DEWR's side to facilitate this process?

short_description: Question about data retention at end of contract
description:
Good Afternoon Information Management Team,

I'm emailing seeking some guidance about data retention/archiving at the end of a contract.  We currently have an engagement with a company called Transitioning Well, who developed and host a website https://smallbusiness.10dayspaidfdvleave.com.au/ to give guidance to small business on the entitlement to 10 days paid family and domestic violence leave. The contract is due to end in November 2026 and there is no further funding available to continue supporting the website. So we are working on a plan to phase it out and re-purpose/archive materials.

Transitioning Well have asked us whether there are any data retention requirements they need to comply with. Under the contract, Transitioning Well own the IP in the materials created - DEWR has a licence to use itWe know the APS needs to comply with the Archives Act and PGPA Act. I've had a look at the contract with Transitioning Well and there's not much in there about records management - only a clause about the supplier not transferring custody of Commonwealth Records without our consent. I've had a look at the Archives Act and it seems that the material prepared for the contract is probably not a Commonwealth Record because it isn't Commonwealth Property (because Transitioning Well owns the IP).

Could you advise us if there are any record keeping/data retention requirements that apply here? Eg: TW need to hold onto copies of the materials created for 7 years. Or in the absence of anything in the contract and the materials meeting any statutory record keeping requirement, is it up to us how we handle the record keeping and archiving? (For your interest, the National Library has partially archived the website on Trove<https://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20251112183854/https:/smallbusiness.10dayspaidfdvleave.com.au/>).

We have copies of things Transitioning Well provided directly to us (quarterly reports, draft content for review etc). But the main output has been the website and its materials (including videos), and things like social media posts and ads to promote the website, which are a little bit tricker to archive.

We appreciate any advice you could give. We're meeting with Transitioning Well next week to discuss so if you could get back to us by Wednesday COB that would be helpful - let us know if that timing works, and happy to discuss.

Kind regards,
Therese

Subject: New Grievance Team Shared Mailbox! [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi Team,

Following the recent updates shared from the Branch business planning underway, I wanted to introduce the new Grievance Team shared mailbox, which is now live!

All feedback, ideas and opportunities to trial different ways of using it are welcome! This initiative is to support our work, and it may take some time to get it right.

PALMGrievance@dewr.gov.au<mailto:PALMGrievance@dewr.gov.au>

Why a shared mailbox?

  *   Having a shared mailbox aligns us with the setup of our sub teams.
  *   It will support continuity of cases (when unexpected leave occurs etc) and improve transparency across the team.
  *   We can build in quickstep templates to assist in responding to common themes (for example: a template when responding to stakeholders requesting assistance without a grievance form etc).


      This initiative also directly supports our branch priorities of:

  *   Consistency - enabling a central point for communication.
  *   Efficiency - improving visibility of work and response.
  *   Reportability - strengthening our ability to track, measure and report on workload (cases, co-ord, briefings etc).

What this means for the team

  *   Please see instructions at the bottom of the email to setup the mailbox - please give me a team's message when you have it setup (reach out if you have any issues).
  *   Starting today can we please CC all grievance related correspondence to the shared mailbox.
     *   I have created individual folders for each of us to file emails on the go.
  *   The mailbox will serve as the primary point for all internal correspondence and case work (our Teams chat remains a pivotal point of for our team communication, and I don't see this changing - unless anyone has any recommendations).
  *   The existing policy of Grievance Forms being directed to PCC and the PALM@dewr email address still stands.
  *   Shared mailbox management can be discussed in the next team meeting once we get a feel for how it will function in our BAU work.

It will take some time to get used to using the shared mailbox, how we use, structure, and operationalise it. If you have any questions or identify opportunities to improve how we use this, please bring it to the team. short_description: Query: Retention of non-compulsory Year 1 test results
description:
Hi team,

We are developing a data retention policy for the Australian Government's Year 1 Phonics Check<https://www.literacyhub.edu.au/plan-teach-and-assess/year-1-phonics-check/> and Number Check.<https://www.mathematicshub.edu.au/plan-teach-and-assess/assessing/y1-number-check/> We are seeking confirmation from Information Management that we can confidently delete the classlists and results once they are no longer used (after 1 year). Could you please advise?

Issue

  *   The Australian Government funds Education Services Australia (ESA) to deliver the Phonics Check and Number Check, which are diagnostic tools for teachers to test Year 1 student knowledge in literacy and numeracy.

  *   The Checks are available for teachers to use online or on paper; they are free and optional to use.
  *   The results help teachers see where to tailor their teaching (eg revisit counting if a student cannot correctly identify how many items are placed in front of them).
  *   For the online option,
     *   Teachers add a classlist to the Check (secure platform behind a log-in) so they can record their students' results.
     *   Classlists and test results are stored on ESA's secure servers within the Check platforms.
     *   Classlists may contain personal information, such as student names and/or student ID numbers; however some teachers use nicknames or numbers for the students in their class.
  *   We are proposing that the online classlists and test results are stored for one year (ie for teacher reference), then deleted.

Important considerations

  *   The information does not constitute a data asset.
  *   Teachers do not report results to the Australian Government; the test is designed for screening/diagnostic use in the classroom. The Australian Government does not produce, monitor or access the information.
  *   As the test is not designed for data collection or analysis, there are no requirements around data integrity (eg some teachers will retest a student a few times over the year to check their progress, so check results, even if they could be collated, could not be used to draw conclusions about or compare cohorts). The classlists and results have no statistical value.
  *   Paper tests are disposed of by the teacher in line with their needs (eg they might destroy it immediately, or keep it in a student's folder for the year that child is in their class). There is no requirement to save, upload or otherwise report the results of the Checks, online or offline.
  *   ESA would continue to retain information about the database as required by the ISM<https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/ism/cyber-security-guidelines/guidelines-for-system-monitoring> and AFDA Express<https://www.naa.gov.au/information-management/records-authorities/types-records-authorities/afda-express-version-2-functions/afda-express-version-2-technology-information-management> (National Archives) ('Records documenting the development, configuration, modification and maintenance of specific software based technology solutions to support agency business')
  *   The department would continue to retain all program records described in the Records Authority<https://www.naa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2019-12/agency-ra-2009-00593947.pdf>, such as those relating to implementation, monitoring, review and administration of the program.

We have already sought advice from

  *   DEWR Cyber Assurance from an ICT security perspective - in favour of disposal as soon as reasonable to minimise the risk of retaining unnecessary (potentially personal) information
  *   National Archives of Australia (regarding AFDA Express and Record Authority requirements) - could not identify for this scenario under the Records Authority

We would be happy to discuss, or facilitate a walk-through of the Checks if this would help.

Please note I am on leave from Friday 5 June, returning Wednesday 10 June.

Many thanks
Ilona

description:
Hi Minh,

When you get a chance, could we please arrange for a duplicate of the "GRANT – Require DUO MFA for W365" policy to be created?

Proposed details:

Policy name: Test Policy: Require MFA for W365
Applications: Same target apps as the existing policy
Target group: Intune – Pilot – Microsoft Authenticator Passkeys – Personal Mobile

Additionally:

Please exclude this group from the existing "GRANT – Require DUO MFA for W365" policy.
If available, could you also configure the sign-in frequency to "Every time" (refer to the attached screenshot)?

Context:

We're testing this configuration as enabling W365 SSO for CPCs requires the removal of Duo for Windows from the CPC device, otherwise it breaks the W365 portal > CPC workflow. In this scenario, the W365 portal becomes the primary control point, so we want to ensure it prompts for authentication on every session, rather than the current 12-hour frequency. I know there was some issues with this in the past so please let me know if this is still the case.

At this stage we don't need to enforce strengths or anything like that on this pilot policy, we just need a separate W365 MFA pilot policy to start our testing. 

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Thanks,
Chris
