short_description: Request for advice - data retention and disposal requirements for data collected through the VET Data Streamlining program national ICT data system.
description:
Hello Information Management team.

I am writing to request some advice on data retention disposal authorities relating to the National Archives Act 1983  (NAA) as it may pertain to the new national VET Data (ICT) System being built to facilitate the VET Data Streamlining (VDS) Program which is anticipated to commence implementation (go-live) from 1 October 2026.

We have previously raised this with the Information Law team, who recommended that we first seek advice from Information Management.

The new ICT system for the VDS Program, known as STARS is being built by the Commonwealth and will collect, store and use data on VET student and training activity. In accordance with s.214B of the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011 (NVETR Act)  operated and maintained by the Commonwealth (via DEWR) in the first instance. However, will allow the DEWR Secretary to transfer the operation and maintenance functions of STARS to the National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) in future.

NCVER have a current Data Retention Policy (extract provided in the Background Information section later in this email), but DEWR is also required to develop the data retention and disposal protocols for the STARS system and these may have a bearing on whether the NCVER policy and associated retention periods outlined are appropriate for the future operation and maintenance of the STARS system.

The STARS system capability relating to data backup, retention, disposal is required to be configured based on the types of data being collected, validated and, in some instances, created by this system and any authorisation under the NAA, Privacy Act 1988 and/or in regard to any obligation by a data custodian of the relevant data set.

While preliminary consideration has been given to this as it pertains to personal information as part of Privacy Impact Assessments (PIA) done for the VDS Program - see background information further down this email - there are recommendations that the obligations under the NAA are further clarified, namely:


  *   whether, and what, data sets/types to be collected by, and held, in STARS are considered 'Commonwealth records' and which data sets/types are not considered 'Commonwealth records'?
  *   whether there is any specific NAA Records Authority that would apply?  Note:  there is a listing of an agency specific records authority  which appears to cover Vocational Education and Training (Department of Education, Employment and Workplace Relations Records Authority.DOC<https://www.naa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2019-12/agency-ra-2009-00593947.pdf>) but it is unclear whether this records authority (specifically at class 20652 for collection, verification and analysis of data, statistics and information) is applicable to our circumstances in relation to collection, validation, disclosure and handling of VET student and training activity data through STARS.
  *   what associated period(s) for retention and archive should apply?

These are the main questions that we are seeking Information Management team's advice on.

To support the Information Management team's consideration of whether, and how, a NAA Records Authority may specifically apply to the STARS system and database settings (as per the questions outlined earlier in this email), we have outlined 4 scenarios of the services/capability that the STARS system will provide:

Scenario 1 - Provisional validation services (optional, and not formally submitted for the Data Provision Requirements (DPRs) under the NVETR Act) - The STARS system capability being implemented will have an optional validation service for Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) to provisionally check that their data records will meet business rules from the new VET Information Standard (VET IS) before they formally submit that data in compliance with the DPRs. This interaction with STARS will be undertaken through Application Program Interfaces (API) technology. Relevant data includes directly uploaded data from the RTO (using a Student Management System), reconciliation reports from validation process / results provided back to RTOs on validation success or errors.

Scenario 2 - jurisdictional -specific data that is covered by the DPRs for some states and territories to have RTOs directly submit to STARS (but which is not part of the national VET data collection that goes to NCVER). - this is data that relates to state and territory contracts with RTOs and will be collected by STARS from RTOs (on behalf of some states and territory training authorities (STAs)) and disclosed back to the relevant STAs for their contractual and funding purposes. The STARS will still run validation rules from the new VET Information Standard where they are applicable for RTOs with contracts/arrangements with particular STAs.  The STAs would be considered data custodians for this type of data. Some data, including data submitted by RTOs and audit logs from validation processes, may need to be retained in STARS for a period to ensure that validation rules for future data submissions can continue to be implemented.

Scenario 3 - national DPRs data set that is collected in STARS for submission to NCVER as per the DPRs under the NVETR Act (and required for national VET Regulator considerations) - this is data that is formally submitted to STARS and which is provided to NCVER in accordance with the DPRs legislative requirements. NCVER is the national VET data custodian for this data and will use the data collected by STARS and validation audit logs/reports to produce VET statistical reports.  NCVER is a not-for-profit company but is contracted by the Commonwealth in relation to its specified role as the national VET data custodian and has legislative obligations set out in the NVETR Act and Student Identifiers Act and Regulations in relation to data disclosures where the data is collected in accordance with the DPRs.

Scenario 4 - System-generated telemetry (audit, business events and performance logging) - data generated by STARS as part of system operations rather than directly submitted VET data (e.g. audit logs of user/system actions, Transaction Batch lifecycle, business event logs capturing processing outcomes, workflow transitions, and performance/diagnostic logs, processing times).  These are created by the STARS system to support accountability, auditability, security monitoring and operational integrity rather than forming part of the VET data collection itself.

The STARS ICT build team have also outlined (see below) some back-up and retention settings being considered but are querying whether the periods of retention are sufficient to meet business requirements and any legislative obligations.  Advice on this is important to determine whether the options need adjustment.

While the STARS system does not currently have any production data in it (and won't until after VDS Program go-live from 1 October 2026), proposed data back-up retention periods for the STARS production database are currently set at:

Short-term retention:

  *   The STARS database can be restored to any point in the last 14 days, accurate to within a few minutes.

Long-term retention

  *   P7W (weekly) - Keep one backup per week for 7 weeks. Provides fine-grained recent recovery points beyond the 14-day short-term window.
  *   P6M (monthly) - Keep one backup per month for 6 months. Useful for recovering from data corruption that went undetected for weeks.
  *   P7Y (yearly) - Keep one backup per year for 7 years. Likely driven by compliance/regulatory requirements for long-term data retention.
  *   week_of_year = 1 - Specifies that the yearly backup is taken from week 1 (i.e. the first week of January). This determines which weekly backup is promoted as the annual snapshot.
  *   immutable_backups = true - Backups cannot be deleted or modified, even by admins. Protects against ransomware and accidental/malicious deletion.

In general, given the potentially high volume and velocity of telemetry data (particularly performance and event logs) and other data in STARS, it will be important to design STARS with an appropriate data lifecycle and storage strategy, including:
*       data partitioning to support efficient querying, retention enforcement and deletion
*       consideration of hot vs cold storage tiers, where:
o   hot storage supports recent and actively queried data
o   cold/archive storage supports longer-term retention at lower cost for compliance and audit purposes (data warehouse)
*       automated archival and disposal processes aligned to retention rules once confirmed


We would appreciate any advice you can provide in respect of the questions as they apply to each of the scenarios presented, and also any associated feedback on the proposed data back-up and retention settings, to assist in clarifying the requirements for the STARS capability build and data lifecycle and storage strategy.

Where possible, can we please request advice by COB Friday 12 June 2026.   Please let us know if there are any issues in meeting this timeframe

We would be happy to arrange a meeting to discuss if that helps.

----

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:

PIA references related to the Archives Act and Privacy Act with regard to retention/deletion/alteration of personal information held in STARS for the purpose of the DPRs.

2022 PIA content (EC25-001534)

Retention of VET Data
For the purposes of APP 11.2, it will be important to determine what personal information within STARS (including in the Staging Database, Master Database, the Data Warehouse, and the various data repositories) is part of a 'Commonwealth record', and therefore subject to the Archives Act 1983 (Cth) (Archives Act), and not required to be deleted once it is no longer required for the purposes for which it was collected.
We suggest that the VET Data Governance Framework set out or reference another document that will set out, as part of the 'data mapping' component, whether the Archives Act applies or if the relevant data custodian is responsible for determining when the VET Data should be deleted.
In addition, if VET Data will be collected by DEWR or the STA systems as part of the validation and quality assurance checks (in Information Flow 4c), it seems to us that the relevant VET Data may not need to be retained for a lengthy period after the validation or quality assurance process was completed (although we acknowledge that retention for a short period may be needed to resolve any errors or discrepancies, and a longer period may be required for audit purposes).

2025 PIA update content (EC25-001534)

13. Amendment and Deletion of Personal Information in STARS
13.1 We understand that the Department is keen to further explore whether, and if so how, it should design STARS to facilitate entities being able to delete VET Data given the application of the Archives Act 1983 (Cth) (Archives Act), and to change/correct VET Data containing personal information if requested by a Student or VET Personnel.
13.2 General privacy best practice principles reflect that individuals should be given as much control over their personal information as is reasonable and practicable in the circumstances. However, there is also recognition that this control needs to be subject to proper record keeping obligations. The nature of the VET Data means that in many circumstances it will be appropriate that records are maintained in a form containing data as it was submitted to STARS, and that it be retained for an extended period of time.
13.3 These principles are reflected in the Privacy Act, in:
13.3.1 APP 11.2, which provides for personal information to be destroyed or de-identified once it is not longer needed for the purposes for which it may be properly used or disclosed - but this obligation does not apply to information that is contained in a 'Commonwealth record' for the purposes of the Archives Act; 7 Section 17, SI Act. 8 See sections 13(3)(a) and 13(4)(a), SI Regulation.
13.3.2 APP 10, which requires reasonable steps to be taken to ensure that personal information being used or disclosed is accurate, up-to-date, complete and relevant (having regard to the purpose of that use or disclosure); and
13.3.3 APP 13, which gives individuals a right to correct their personal information, but this is limited to taking steps that are 'reasonable in the circumstances'.
13.4 However, not all entities that will be data custodians of VET Data in STARS will be bound by the Privacy Act. If Recommendation 7 in the Original PIA, and Recommendation 2 and Recommendation 3 in this PIA Update report, are implemented, it will be clear which data custodians have effective control over the various VET Data sets stored in STARS. It follows that those entities will be responsible for applying the privacy and record-keeping obligations which apply to them, in relation to the VET Data within their control. For example, entities subject to the Archives Act will not need to delete personal information if the VET Data is considered to be stored in a 'Commonwealth record', but such entities should ensure that there is an appropriate records disposal or other authority in place to permit any required deletion (as discussed in the Original PIA).
13.5 It will be important that the Department designs and builds STARS so that all data custodians can take actions to delete or correct the VET Data within their effective control. Whether or not a data custodian takes those actions in a particular circumstance will depend on the legislation that applies to that entity (e.g. the requirements of either the Privacy Act and Archives Act, or the applicable State/Territory privacy and record-keeping legislation). The Department may also wish to consult with the proposed data custodians to determine whether data custodians would prefer that STARS be configured so that only certain STARS Users from that entity are permitted to delete or correct the VET Data.
13.6 We also observe that it would be privacy enhancing if there were protocols agreed by the Department, NCVER, VET Regulators, STAs, and the SI Registrar for the handling of requests to correct personal information.
13.7 Accordingly, this issue raises the following privacy risk:
Privacy Risk 3: The arrangements for STARS may not permit effective management by data custodians of any requests by Students or VET Personnel for correction of their personal information stored in STARS, or other applicable record-keeping obligations.
13.8 Recommendation 5 is a new recommendation designed to address this risk.

Summary of findings and recommendations
Deletion or correction of VET Data
3.15 It would be consistent with privacy principles for Students to be given as much control as possible over their personal information stored in STARS, and for entities to take steps to correct information to ensure that it is accurate, complete and up-to-date. However, the principles behind the Privacy Act (as reflected in State and Territory privacy regimes) also recognise that these principles need to be subject to proper record-keeping obligations. The nature of the VET Data means that it will be appropriate in many circumstances for personal information in records to be maintained as it was submitted to STARS, and retained for an extended period of time.
3.16 We consider that it is appropriate for STARS to be designed and built with functionality that will allow each data custodian to take action as is required by the privacy and record-keeping obligations that apply to that entity, including in response to Students or VET Personnel requesting correction or deletion of their personal information.
3.17 In addition, it would reflect privacy best practice for there to be clear protocols between all data custodians for managing requests for correction of personal information in STARS, to manage the following privacy risk: Privacy Risk 3: The arrangements for STARS may not permit effective management by data custodians of any requests by Students or VET Personnel for correction of their personal information stored in STARS, or other applicable record-keeping obligations.

3.18 Accordingly, we make the following new recommendation:

CAUTION: This email originated from outside of the organisation. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognise the sender and know the content is safe.


OFFICIAL



OFFICIAL

Dear Emissions Reporters,
We are writing to let you know that all Commonwealth entities will use the Emissions Data Portal for 2025-26 emissions reporting. The portal supports the same Microsoft Excel-based Emissions Reporting Tool (ERT) process you already use but provides a more secure and efficient way to submit data, receive feedback and access outputs.
No immediate action is required at this stage. This email outlines what is changing, what will stay the same, and the key dates and actions to be aware of. We will provide the information you need to prepare closer to launch.
What you need to know

  *   What stays the same: you will continue to complete your activity data using the Microsoft Excel-based Emissions Reporting Tool (ERT).
  *   What changes: instead of exchanging the ERT by email, you will upload it through the portal and download validated outputs and reports from the portal.
  *   Why this matters: the portal provides a secure and more efficient way to manage submissions, receive validation feedback and track progress through to approval.
Key dates and required actions

  *   3 June 2026 - Webinar: an overview and demonstration of the portal. Please attend.
  *   15 June 2026 - Whitelisting: Confirm with your IT team that the required portal URL and tenant have been allowed on your network.
  *   17 June 2026 - User access request form due: Submit your completed user access request form<https://forms.office.com/r/PLpu5AcHyX> by this date (limited to 4 per entity).
  *   1 July 2026 - Portal go-live: Begin using the Emissions Data Portal for 2025-26 emissions reporting. The portal will be the required submission channel for all entities from this date.
  *   From July 2026 - Onboarding and support: Guidance, onboarding materials and support will be provided to reporting entities and delegates.
Whitelisting requirements
To support access to the portal, please work with your IT team to ensure the required tenant and portal URL are allowed on your network. The portal uses the same platform as the Central Budget Management System (CBMS), which may assist your IT team with this process. Please request the following:

  *   Whitelist the following Azure tenancy
     *   appsfinancegovau.onmicrosoft.com
     *   Tenant ID: af3f30c5-7e9e-42d8-84d0-f85676b5fe1e
  *   Allow access to the portal which will be available at the endpoint: https://netzero.portal.finance.gov.au<https://netzero.portal.finance.gov.au/>
What to expect from the portal
The portal will allow you to download the ERT, upload completed files, receive validation feedback, access reports and support online approval by your entity's nominated delegate. It is intended to make the reporting process easier to manage, while maintaining the reporting approach entities already know.
We recognise this is a change to the current process and will provide support to help entities transition to the portal. If you have any questions in the meantime, please contact us.
If you haven't received the invite to the Webinar through GovTEAMS, please response to EmissionsAccounting@finance.gov.au<mailto:EmissionsAccounting@finance.gov.au>

Kind regards
Donna

short_description: Request for advice on record retention and disposal obligations under TRA Deed expiry
description:
Hi team,

Unsure if I have the correct team here, but we have been advised to engage with the department's Information Management and SharePoint team following some recent legal advice.
Appreciative of any support you can provide if this is not the correct business area.

I am seeking your advice on an upcoming contract closure for the Job Ready Program within the Trades Recognition Australia branch.

The matter relates to the handling of Deed Material and Confidential Information for external Providers.

By way of background, the Deed requires Providers to retain records in accordance with for a period of 7 years following expiry.
While the department may issue directions to Providers to return or destroy Deed Material and Confidential Information at expiry, Providers must retain sufficient records to remain compliant with those obligations.

We have been advised that a significant portion of this material is likely to constitute 'Commonwealth records' under the Archives Act 1983.
This includes reporting outputs and associated documentation.
As a result, we have been strongly advised to contact you as any direction to return/destroy material would need to align with the Act, noting that destruction is only permitted where authorised by the National Archives or under an approved disposal authority.

For context, the key deliverables captured under these include:

  *   Workplace Assessment Reports
  *   Review Assessment Reports
  *   Monthly Provider Reports
  *   Annual Provider Report
  *   All information and material on the JRP website (does not exist)
  *   general information about the services relating to the Workplace Asessment Serivces of the Job Ready Program that we may supply to you for your website (does not exist)
  *   JRP Guidelines
  *   Workplace Assessment Guidelines


In addition, we note that under clause G.2, "Excluded Material" includes promotional, delivery and assessment tools developed by Providers using their own resources, which may affect what can or should be returned or destroyed.

Importantly all of the listed deliverables above are all digital only copies and the department expects to hold exact copies of all deliverables at the point of Deed expiry.
With this said even if providers destroyed/returned copies at a later date, TRA would still have copies of these records.

Given this context, we are seeking your advice on:

  1.  The appropriate approach to directing Providers on the return and or destruction of Deed Material and Confidential Information at Deed expiry.
  2.  Any specific Archives Act obligations or constraints we must apply, particularly in relation to reporting outputs and associated records.
  3.  How to manage situations where Providers are required to retain records for the 7-year period, including whether duplication (department-held vs provider-held records) raises any issues.
  4.  The recommended approach for material that Providers retain beyond expiry, including expectations once the 7-year retention period concludes.
  5.  Any preferred wording, templates or guidance for communicating clear instructions to Providers.

We are aiming to provide clear and compliant directions to Providers, and to avoid any ambiguity at contract closure.
Please let me know if you require any further information.

Kind regards,
Shaun

Alert Signal
BEEP BEEP BEEP
All staff to secure sensitive materials

All wardens to attend to emergency procedures

All others to follow local procedures and
await instructions

description:
**************************************************************************
CAUTION: This email originated from outside of the organisation. Do not click links or open attachments unless you recognise the sender and know the content is safe.
**************************************************************************

OFFICIAL

Our reference: 2023/471; 2026/1184444
Records Management Section
Department of Education, Employment and Workplace Relations
Request under Section 40 of the Archives Act 1983
for Records Not Recorded in Archival Custody (NRA)

On 9 March 2026, a researcher applied under Section 40 of the Archives Act 1983, for open period records. Please see attachments for details.

Legislative background
Section 40 Applications for access to records
            (1)  This section applies in relation to an application to the Archives for access, or for an extension of partial access, to a record referred to in section 31
Section 31 (1A) This section applies to a Commonwealth record that:
(a)  is in the open access period; and
(b)  is in the care of the Archives or in the custody of a Commonwealth institution; and
(c)  is not an exempt record.
Section 31(2) requires agencies that have custody of open period records to make whatever arrangements are necessary to enable the Archives to meet its obligations in Section 31(1).

If records are located
If records are located that match the application they should be transferred to the Team Leader Research Centre at the National Archives in Canberra. Please enclose a covering letter titled 'Temporary reference transfer for Section 40 Application' and quote our Access Application Job no. 2026/1184444.
Our preference is to receive any records located in the format they were created. Please also include details of the Commonwealth Record Series and file number (control symbol).

If the record/s are digital copies or in a digital format, please contact me to discuss delivery options. Do not email digital records.

If the record/s contains any security classification markers, please contact me to discuss delivery options.

If no records are located, or they have been destroyed
If no records can be located in response to the application, please advise the National Archives of the details of the searches that were undertaken to locate the record for example:
*     * Search terms used to locate relevant records in EDRMS systems
*     * EDRMS and databases searched, and
*         * The details of any physical control records searched e.g. index cards.

If records relevant to the application have been destroyed, please advise the
*     * Records Authority number (or Administrative Functions Disposal Authorities (AFDA), Functional Records Disposal Authorities (FRDA), General records authorities (GRAs) Records Disposal Authorities (RDAs), Records Disposal Schedules (RDS, General Disposal Authorities and General Disposal Schedules (GDA/GDS))
*     * the class the records were sentenced under, and
*         * the date of destruction

short_description: Inquiry: Status and Process for Formalising Qualtrics Data Retention & Collection Policy
description:
Hi Julie,

I'm reaching out to understand the current status and process for progressing the formalisation of the department's data retention and collection policy for Qualtrics.

I understand that my previous EL1, Kristy Kelly, had commenced work in this space prior to her departure, and I'm keen to pick up where things left off or understand what next steps are required to get this moving again.

At present, the guidance we have been providing to users is that Qualtrics is not an approved system for long-term recordkeeping. As such, projects that collect participant responses are expected to export their data and store it in an approved departmental system such as Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint Online. We also advise that data should not be retained indefinitely within Qualtrics, and that any extended analysis should be conducted outside the platform.

However, this guidance is not yet formally documented as policy (to my knowledge), and I'm increasingly being asked to provide definitive advice to users. It would be helpful to understand:

  *   Whether there is an existing draft policy or guidance in development
  *   Where the work currently sits in terms of review or approval
  *   What the process and timelines are for formalising this
  *   How I can support progressing this work (if required)

Having a formalised position will help ensure we are providing consistent and compliant advice across the department.

Thanks in advance for your assistance, and please let me know if it would be easier to discuss via a teams call.

Kind regards,

Josh Ryder

Hi Cathie,

Thank you for providing FWO's proposed conditions for reactivation of the emergency access card.

We appreciate FWO's willingness to work toward a solution and acknowledge the PSPF obligations that FWO must meet. We are committed to finding arrangements that satisfy both building safety requirements and FWO's security obligations.

We note that the following aspects of your proposed conditions have always been in place and have operated successfully throughout FWO's tenancy from 2015 to April 2026 without any security incidents:

  *   Outside business hours: The emergency access card was only ever used for genuine emergency situations (Fire/Ambulance/Police escort, critical safety systems, flooding, structural issues, immediate risk to life/safety/property).
  *   During business hours: Building management has always followed FWO visitor management procedures - signing in and being escorted when accessing office areas.
  *   Emergency access card usage: The card has only ever been used outside business hours when FWO staff were not in attendance for emergency situations and during business hours.

These arrangements worked effectively for over 10 years. The issues we are now experiencing stem from the card's deactivation, not from any misuse or breach of these established protocols.

However, we have identified several concerns with the proposed conditions that require clarification:

1. Definition of "Emergency" - Outside Business Hours:
While we agree with the core emergency scenarios you've outlined, the definition needs to include building system emergencies that don't necessarily pose immediate risk to life but do require urgent access to prevent property damage, maintain essential services, or meet regulatory compliance. Examples include:

  *   Electronic security system failures (as experienced on 11 May 2026)
  *   HVAC system failures affecting critical equipment or server rooms
  *   Building Management System (BMS) failures requiring immediate rectification
  *   Electrical system faults requiring immediate isolation and investigation
  *   Equipment failures requiring urgent replacement to restore building services
  *   Water leaks requiring urgent investigation and isolation (e.g., leaking pipes in ceiling spaces, leaking air conditioning units, plumbing failures affecting FWO tenancy)
Proposed Amendment: "Emergency access includes situations requiring immediate attendance by emergency services, critical safety system failures, flooding, structural issues, immediate risk to life/safety/property damage, and building system failures requiring immediate investigation and rectification to maintain building safety, security, and essential services."

2. Business Hours Access - Service Areas vs Office Areas:
We note your requirement for sign-in and escort during business hours. We agree with this requirement when accessing FWO office areas and service areas, and will continue to follow this protocol. However, in the past there were situations where FWO staff were not available to provide escorts, and when urgent access needs to be provided, we need to clarify access to building service areas, which include:

  *   Plant rooms
  *   Ceiling spaces and service voids
  *   Service cabinets and electrical cupboards
  *   Riser cupboards
  *   Communications rooms
Proposed Clarification: The emergency access card (which is held in the building security office in a locked cabinet) used to access building service areas and plant rooms for urgent situations during business hours may proceed with Base Building Security escort but without FWO staff (if not available), with all access logged. Sign-in and escort will continue to be required for access to FWO office areas as per current practice.

- Preproduction: EPPEAPP210 (pprod.construction.enet)

The user can successfully access production shared folders on:
- EPREAPP212 (application.enet)

The following checks were completed from the Cloud PC:
1. DNS resolution is working correctly (EDEIAPP202 resolves to 10.11.62.170)
2. ICMP (ping) fails
3. TCP connectivity on port 445 fails (Test-NetConnection unsuccessful)
4. SMB share enumeration fails (System error 53: Network path not found)
5. Production server access (EPREAPP212) works from the same Cloud PC

These results indicate a network connectivity issue between the Cloud PC subnet (10.82.64.0/xx) and the preproduction and development server. DNS resolution is confirmed, but there is no network path (ICMP or TCP 445) to the lower environment servers.

This sounds very similar to a change request Digital Collabortions raised for Content Manager (CHG0057766). 

Could you please advise:
1. The appropriate change request template required to enable connectivity
2. The specific source details needed (e.g. Cloud PC subnet, individual IP, or service tag)

short_description: Enhancements to SARs and resource membership records on ServiceNow
description:
Hi,

I have a few questions for the ServiceNow team regarding our existing SARs (non-exhaustive):

  *   APP_DAP_Data_ECEC_PROD
  *   APP_DAP_Data_ECEC_Specific_PROD
  *   APP_DAP_Data_ECEC_Business_PROD
  *   APP_DAP_Data_ECEC_EXP

To help us meet auditing requirements, we're looking to enhance these and wanted to check what might be possible.

1. Updates to the SAR forms
We're hoping to explore whether the following improvements can be made:

  *   Allow users to upload attachments (e.g. training records and security clearances)
  *   Include or expand terms and conditions, where needed
  *   Add additional approval tiers, with streamlined workflows where appropriate
  *   Introduce access expiry dates, along with automated reminder emails for re-application
We're happy to provide more detailed requirements if that would help.

2. Access to user records to conduct quality assurance
We would also like to understand what information is available on users who currently have access, including:

  *   SAR form details (including the business case)
  *   Access start and expiry dates (expiry dates will need to be configured)
  *   Security clearance information
  *   Approval details (who approved access)
  *   Confirmation that records are retained appropriately and are tamper-resistant
  *   Ability to provide records for auditors with minimal manual effort.
I'm aware that the Corporate Directory can provide information on membership for a resource but it doesn't currently contain these granular details.

Could you please let us know:

  *   Whether the updates in point 1 are feasible
  *   Whether the records in point 2 are available in a way that we can easily access.

Subject: SWA Databricks to PBI service connection query [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Good afternoon all,
Reaching out to you all as I know you've all been able to help the SWA Data team out in the past with our Power BI and DataBricks infrastructure. We've had a lot of success transitioning our data compilation from PBI dataflows into DataBricks workbooks with results stored in managed tables on Unity Catalogue. Processes that were taking us days in PBI are now completed in less than 10 minutes in DataBricks.
The last piece of the puzzle we're now grappling with is connecting our DataBricks results to existing reporting in PBI service.
Specifically, we want to use a dataflow in PBI service to import a relatively small Unity Catalogue table (4 million rows, DataBricks claims size is 173.2MiB). The problem where having is that while this import runs in 2 minutes on PBI desktop, in PBI service the dataflow often spins forever (we've been cancelling after 10 hours of non-responsiveness).
We're uncertain what is causing these performance issues but have a few suspicions that we wanted to run by you:
Tweaking the gateway
In PBI Service we use the SWA_ADB_DIA_PROD shared service PROD PBI gateway to connect to DataBricks. At the moment this gateway uses an all-purpose compute in our DataBricks environment rather than a serverless SQL warehouse compute. It's our understanding that the latter may be better suited to the task and we now have this setup in DataBricks so we could switch it over. Whilst we can set this up in Databricks, we would require the gateway to be adjusted so this can be enabled.
Alternatively, we thought the gateway might not be configured to best meet the requirement however this seems unlikely given using the gateway on PBI desktop works without issues with data of this size.
Gen2 Dataflow
Our other thought was that we may need to tweak our PBI workspace to enable Dataflow Gen2 rather than the Dataflow Gen1 (legacy) we are currently relying on. Our reading suggests Dataflow Gen 1 has some issues and Dataflow Gen2 may be better suited to this task. However we don't have the permissions to upgrade the PBI service workspace on our end, when we try and create a  Dataflow Gen2 we get the error
Unable to create Dataflow Gen2
Creating Dataflow Gen2 isn't currently supported in this workspace. Ask your Fabric admin to turn on settings allowing users to start Fabric trials and to create Dataflow Gen2, and then try again.
We'd be keen to meet and discuss this issue further in efforts to isolate where the problem is and figure out what we need to do to move forward.
Best,
Rhys O'Neill
Safe Work Australia

Data Improvement & Analysis | Assistant Director
Evidence, Communications & Industries Policy

short_description: Inquiry: Status and Process for Formalising Qualtrics Data Retention & Collection Policy
description:
Hi team,

I'm reaching out to understand the current status and process for progressing the formalisation of the department's data retention and collection policy for Qualtrics.

I understand that my previous EL1, Kristy Kelly, had commenced work in this space prior to her departure, and I'm keen to pick up where things left off or understand what next steps are required to get this moving again.

At present, the guidance we have been providing to users is that Qualtrics is not an approved system for long-term recordkeeping. As such, projects that collect participant responses are expected to export their data and store it in an approved departmental system such as Content Manager, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint Online. We also advise that data should not be retained indefinitely within Qualtrics, and that any extended analysis should be conducted outside the platform.

However, this guidance is not yet formally documented as policy (to my knowledge), and I'm increasingly being asked to provide definitive advice to users. It would be helpful to understand:

  *   Whether there is an existing draft policy or guidance in development
  *   Where the work currently sits in terms of review or approval
  *   What the process and timelines are for formalising this
  *   How I can support progressing this work (if required)

Having a formalised position will help ensure we are providing consistent and compliant advice across the department.

Thanks in advance for your assistance, and please let me know if it would be easier to discuss via a teams call.

Kind regards,

Josh Ryder

Project Officer

Enterprise Technology Division

Today I am very pleased to launch the Department's new Evaluation, Research and Evidence Framework.

For a department such as ours, it is vitally important that we invest in evaluation, research and evidence. The investment supports high-quality policy development, ensures our policies are aligned with the priorities of the Government and meet the needs of employers, employees and job seekers. It provides us with the insight to plan for the future. And it holds us accountable to the Australian public.

This Department has a strong tradition of excellence in evaluation, research and evidence and we should always aspire to build on our strengths. That's why the Framework sets out a forward plan to strengthen the evidence base that will help us deliver on our priorities into the future. I was particularly pleased to see how well the Framework supports the themes of collaboration, people, delivery and a forward-looking approach that underpin our Strategic Plan. 

The Framework will focus our work under the four pillars of evaluation, research, data management and enhanced capability. For this to be a success it will need the skills and expertise of people across the Department working in virtual teams. Getting involved in these teams will provide staff with the opportunity to shape creative solutions and I encourage anyone who is interested in being part of these projects to speak to their managers. 

I would like to congratulate everyone who was involved in developing this important document. It will make it easier for our people to find and use evidence, and improve our already enviable standards and ethics.

Renée Leon

The error message indicates that something needs to be enabled at Azure AD:

To resolve the AADSTS700054 error, you need to enable the Implicit grant flow for ID tokens in your Azure app registration. This error occurs because your application is requesting an ID token, but the app registration isn't configured to issue them through the authorization endpoint. [1<https://build5nines.com/fix-response_type-id_token-is-not-enabled-for-the-application-aadsts700054/>, 2<https://www.koskila.net/how-to-fix-aadsts700054-response_type-id_token-is-not-enabled-for-the-application-error/>]
How to Fix the Error

  1.  Open your App Registration: Sign in to the Azure Portal and navigate to Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) > App registrations.
  2.  Select your Application: Find and click on the name of the application that is causing the error.
  3.  Navigate to Authentication: In the left-hand menu under the Manage section, click on Authentication.
  4.  Enable ID Tokens:
     *   Scroll down to the section titled Implicit grant and hybrid flows.
     *   Check the box for ID tokens (used for implicit and hybrid flows).
     *   (Optional) If your app also requires access tokens via this flow, check the Access tokens box as well.
  5.  Save Changes: Click the Save button at the top of the page. [1<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-authentication-provider-aad>, 2<https://www.drillster.com/info/developers/integration-types/open-id-connect/ms-entra-id/>, 3<https://forum.uipath.com/t/error-aadsts700054-response-type-id-token-is-not-enabled-for-the-application-when-logging-into-orchestrator-with-azure-ad/345384>, 4<https://softchief.com/2021/08/18/solved-response_type-token-is-not-enabled-for-the-application-in-dynamics-365-and-postman-connection/>, 5<https://docs.azure.cn/en-us/container-apps/authentication-entra>, 6<https://build5nines.com/fix-response_type-id_token-is-not-enabled-for-the-application-aadsts700054/>]
Troubleshooting Tips

  *   Redirect URI Platform: Ensure you have a platform configuration added (like Web or SPA). If no platform is configured, the implicit grant options may be hidden.
  *   Propagation Time: It may take a minute or two for these changes to take effect across Microsoft's servers. Try signing in again after a short wait or use an incognito/private browser window to avoid caching issues.
  *   Security Best Practice: If your application supports the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE (standard for modern Single Page Apps), Microsoft recommends using that instead of the Implicit Flow for better security. [1<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/886555/aadsts700054-response-type-id-token-is-not-enabled>, 2<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/questions/886555/aadsts700054-response-type-id-token-is-not-enabled>, 3<https://kb.total-view.com/2024sp1/documentation/authentication/add-office-365-authentication.html>, 4<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/892629/response-type-id-token-is-not-enabled-for-the-appl>]


Error AADSTS50105 occurs in Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) when a user tries to sign in to an application, but their IT administrator has configured the app to block users unless they are explicitly granted access. [1<https://support.digitaltheatreplus.com/resolving-microsoft-aadsts50105-error>, 2<https://admindroid.com/entra-id-sign-in-error-50105-user-not-assigned-to-enterprise-app>]
What the Error Means
This error means the signed-in account is blocked for one of two reasons:

  1.  The user's specific email/account is not directly assigned to the application in the Microsoft Entra admin portal.
  2.  The user is not a member of a group that has been granted permission to access the application. [1<https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/AADSTS50105-Your-administrator-has-configured-the-application-Autodesk-SSO-to-block-users-unless-they-are-specifically-granted-assigned-access-to-the-application-appears-when-login-into-Autodesk-Single-Sign-On.html>, 2<https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-cloud/kb/error-aadsts50105-encountered-when-logging-into-atlassian-cloud/>, 3<https://support.digitaltheatreplus.com/resolving-microsoft-aadsts50105-error>]
How to Fix It
Because this is an access control policy, end-users cannot fix this themselves. It requires action from an IT or Application Administrator using the Microsoft Entra admin center: [1<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/answers/questions/5840591/i-donot-have-admin-access-to-add-user-to-the-enter>, 2<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5840591/i-donot-have-admin-access-to-add-user-to-the-enter>, 3<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/answers/questions/2183708/i-have-entra-federated-with-okta-one-of-my-users-i>, 4<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5854940/cannot-close-microsoft-account-organization-blocke>, 5<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5840591/i-donot-have-admin-access-to-add-user-to-the-enter>]
